newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF says Bulgaria must complete structural reform.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Bulgaria must complete structural reform.

text.p: The success of a currency board plan, due to be introduced in Bulgaria next year to boost confidence in the crumbling lev, depends on fulfilment of structural reform commitments, IMF officials said on Friday.
"The structural reform remains a very strong issue as the whole restructuring package relies also on World Bank funds," an International Monetary Fund official who declined to be named told Reuters.
Failure to meet reform targets including the closing or restructuring of some 2,060 state loss-making enterprises has led to the suspension of funding from the World Bank and the IMF.

Two IMF technical missions spent 10 days in Sofia to help the government prepare the legal adjustments for restructuring the central bank into a currency board and to help draft the 1997 budget projections.

The currency board is a form of fixed exchange rate regime which requires that levs in circulation and commercial banks' mimimum reserves at the central bank match central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves.
The central bank, which will also be banned from lending to the government and commercial banks, will be transformed into two departments -- a currency board and a bank supervision division.

The government had accepted the plan saying the system would be introduced after parliament passes next year's budget and a package of legal amendments which would make the currency board operational.
An IMF negotiatiating mission is expected to arrive in January and finalise the deal, afer the legal adjustments have been passed in parliament.
IMF officials did not reveal any of the budget parameters, but Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Thursday that next year's budget assumption for the lev/dollar rate was between 400 and 500.
